minutes.headline: Task force voted to draft a support letter for a 604B watershed grant and set dates for FinCom, Select Board and a public session.
minutes.summary: The task force compared funding stormwater work through a utility versus the operating budget, discussing staffing (a junior engineer or project manager, partly shared with DPW), outsourcing versus hiring, and the effect on resident bills. It scheduled presentations (Select Board Oct 20, FinCom Oct 22) and a public info session Nov 9 at the library's Wallace room. It reviewed draft fee and abatement slides and the 604B grant, then voted on a support letter and minutes.

budget_items.topic: Stormwater budget, utility vs operating budget
budget_items.what_was_said: A new column shows the operating-budget version; the utility version needs more because of administrative overhead.
A share of the director's salary is charged to the program, with a utility at a larger share than the operating option.
The two approaches differ only by administrative overhead, and the work cost is the same.
The two bottom-line figures were read aloud for the utility and operating versions.

budget_items.topic: Tax bill impact if in the operating budget
budget_items.what_was_said: Using a Prop 2.5 calculator on the FY26 rate, the impact on the average single-family bill was estimated and noted as growing at the levy cap.
Consultant rates were put well above the loaded cost of an in-house hire.
Residents would pay a smaller amount under the utility than the operating budget despite the larger total.
Fee would come in under the advertised cap, likely a bit lower with a revised budget.
One equivalent residential unit per home with a fixed annual fee not to exceed a cap for the first three years.
Another town's fee and enterprise fund were compared, with budget tiers described.
The state grant is funded fully with no match this year, and a related 319 program is also without a match.

what_happened.line: The task force voted 4-0 by roll call to have the consultant draft a letter of support for a 604B watershed grant application, to be signed electronically.
Dates were set: Select Board presentation Oct 20, FinCom Oct 22, and a public info session Monday Nov 9 at 7 p.m. in the library's Wallace room.
The task force compared funding stormwater through a utility versus the operating budget; the two differ in administrative overhead, not in the cost of the work.
State and charitable properties will be left out of fee billing, and the abatement review interval will change from 10 years toward 3.
A virtual slide review was set for Thursday Oct 15, with slides going to the boards by the end of Friday Oct 16 or over the weekend.

why_it_matters: Whether stormwater is paid through a separate utility fee or through the tax levy decides how the cost lands on a household's bill, and residents will hear both options before any vote on one.

The task force has not yet chosen between the two, and the fee design (exempt properties, abatement interval) is still being revised, so the terms residents are shown in November may differ from the current drafts.
